caption:
The CSA’s recently reached out with a killer side quest for me in the post-Olympic period of rot. They wanted a narrative sketch that focused on our current hockey movie renaissance and pay a tribute to Icon Award winner @mikemyers. After watching through his filmography, “Wayne’s World” naturally stuck out - but specifically AS a hockey movie. And Mike Myers conceding the point on national television, I will tell to strangers in bars for my remaining days. 

@jessica_capo was the mastermind and she’s responsible for all the pieces coming together. She’s a mentor and big sister, I owe her so much.

@andrewventura & @aaronsambeyfilm are such talents who elevate everything I fumble through. Thanks for being down to make a little movie in my driveway with Canada’s best on little notice. And @ruskaycolour for always fixing our mistakes in the field.

Here’s an interesting “hockey pond” story. I’m from a very small cluster of towns in Newfoundland. I played high school sports, not hockey, with this girl for years. She is 3 years older than me and left the town after school. I saw her briefly about 10 years later. She almost made the 🇨🇦 hockey team but this other player you may have heard of, Danielle Goyette, made the team. Haven’t seen her in 15 years. But I since heard about this story. She was 9 and skating, carrying and shooting the puck on net on the local pond. Typical hockey player. There was only one other person, a 6 year old boy just playing on the other side. She saw him there and glanced over a few times. When she looked again, he was gone. She looked around the shore and didn’t see him. Looked back, his head popped up out of the water. The ice crashed through. She skated as fast as possible then the ice started to crack and break under her. She crawled to him and called out his name. Eventually she was close enough to stretch her stick so he could grab it. He fell through again but with her encouragement and endronine strength pulled him up. She crawled with him towards the shore and she held him in her arms and she crashed through the ice close to the shore. Fortunately she did not fall, only stumbled. Since she was skating on the other side, she only had her skates with no skate guards. She carried him (a 9 year old girl carrying a 6 year old boy) over the rocky brook that streamed down a steep long hill. Eventually, she reached their town. She carried him to his mothers house and walked home. Collectively it was about a kilometre walk. Well, she was the youngest person to receive the 🇨🇦medal of bravery and the St. John’s Ambulance had a similar award.  Us Newfoundlanders do not think of anything as “heroic” You’re there, someone needs help, you help them, no big deal. The “town’s” story was this boy fell through through the ice, someone was there, he’s OK. I had no idea it was her and none of our teammates in any of the four sports knew.
